metadata.description: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

CS 1301.name: Introduction to Computing
CS 1301.description: Introduction to computing principles and programming practices with an emphasis on the design, construction and implementation of problem solutions use of software tools.

CS 1331.name: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming
CS 1331.description: Introduction to techniques and methods of object-oriented programming such as encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. Emphasis on software development and individual programming skills.

CS 1332.name: Data Structures and Algorithms for Applications
CS 1332.description: Computer data structures and algorithms in the context of object-oriented programming. Focus on software development towards applications.

CS 2050.name: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
CS 2050.description: Proof methods, strategy, correctness of algorithms over discrete structures. Induction and recursion. Complexity and order of growth. Number theoretic principles and algorithms. Counting and computability.

CS 2110.name: Computer Organization and Programming
CS 2110.description: An introduction to basic computer hardware, machine language, assembly language, and C programming.

CS 2200.name: Computer Systems and Networks
CS 2200.description: A broad exposure to computer system structure and networking including software abstractions in operating systems for orchestrating the usage of the computing resources.

CS 2316.name: Data Manipulation for Science and Industry
CS 2316.description: Reading, manipulating, and exporting data for engineering, business, and scientific applications. Covers GUI's, File I/O, basic SQL, and web scraping.

CS 2340.name: Objects and Design
CS 2340.description: Object-oriented programming methods for dealing with large programs. Focus on quality processes, effective debugging techniques, and testing to assure a quality product.

CS 3510.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
CS 3510.description: Basic techniques of design and analysis of efficient algorithms for standard computational problems. NP-Completeness.

CS 3600.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
CS 3600.description: An introduction to artificial intelligence and machine learning. Topics include intelligent system design methodologies, search and problem solving, supervised and reinforced learning.

CS 3210.name: Design of Operating Systems
CS 3210.description: Operating systems concepts, including multi-threading, scheduling, synchronization, communication, and access control. Projects will cover design and implementation of several operating systems components.

CS 3251.name: Computer Networking I
CS 3251.description: Introduction to problems in computer networking, including error recovery, medium access, routing, flow control, and transport. Emphasis on current best practice. Includes programming of networked applications.

CS 3451.name: Computer Graphics
CS 3451.description: Geometric constructions; transformations; perception; reflection models; photorealistic; non-photorealistic, and image-based rendering.

CS 4400.name: Introduction to Database Systems
CS 4400.description: Comprehensive coverage of mainstream database concepts such as the entity-relationship model, relational databases, query languages, and database design methodology.

CS 4641.name: Machine Learning
CS 4641.description: Machine learning techniques and applications. Topics include foundational issues; inductive, analytical, numerical, and theoretical approaches; and real-world applications.

CS 4476.name: Introduction to Computer Vision
CS 4476.description: Introduction to computer vision including fundamentals of image formation, camera imaging geometry, feature detection and matching, stereo, motion estimation and tracking.

CS 4455.name: Video Game Design and Programming
CS 4455.description: Techniques for electronic game design and programming, including graphics game engines, motion generation, behavioral control for autonomous characters.

CS 4650.name: Natural Language Understanding
CS 4650.description: Methodologies for designing systems that comprehend natural language. Topics include lexical analysis, parsing, interpretation of sentences, semantic representation.
